color_exactness_applicability.mechanism: bullet3 TinyRenderer's MULTIPLICATIVE one-light law out_i = int(255*c_i*(A + D*max(0,n.l) + S*max(0,r_z)**spec)*L_i), truncated, A=0.6 D=0.35 S=0.05 spec=2, light (-50,30,100) normalised, no shadow, no gamma
color_exactness_applicability.official_renderer_evidence: the official PyFlyt 0.29.0 / pybullet 3.2.7 frame's brightest body pixel is 0.991*int(255*c); the requested triple is absent from the OFFICIAL frames too
color_exactness_applicability.scope_note: scoped to these five lit leaves only; any other RGB leaf on this env stays judged against literal equality
color_exactness_applicability.status: not_applicable: literal RGB equality is unreachable under the reference's own law
color_exactness_applicability.successor: PROPOSAL only, not implemented and not mandatory: compare this renderer's response to the knob against the OFFICIAL renderer's response to the same knob

PFRocketLanding.documented_limitations: nvdiff's CPU transform is batch-size invariant to within one float32 ulp at every width, and bitwise at every width on arm64; on x86-64 the clip positions move by one ulp at widths 1-6 and the normals at widths 4 and 8 (CLOSURE-1). Cuda, the certified device, is bitwise invariant at every width. No frame this cell produces is affected: device='cpu' raises. See findings.md section M7 and examples/results/step7/rocket-landing/closure1/.

visual_fidelity.measured_at: 480 px, supersample 1, default appearance, worst of 4 independent 64-state draws of sample_states (default_rng(1000..1003)) over the rows the reference bridge reaches, against PyFlyt 0.29.0 / pybullet 3.2.7 TinyRenderer frames of swm/PFRocketLanding-v0 at the lagged pose; NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 gpu2106, SLURM job 6410105, tree 726241e, torch 2.14.0+cu126, nvdiffrast 0.4.0 (scratch/step7/rocket-landing/measure_tier.py, examples/results/step7/rocket-landing/tier/job6410105/)

PFRocketLanding.visual_note: A different rasterizer (nvdiffrast) drawing TinyRenderer's scene under TinyRenderer's law. Residual: silhouette pixels (different edge rules and float paths), checker-tile edges (sub-pixel UV rounding under nearest sampling) and the far ground where tiles are sub-pixel, scipy's rather than Bullet's triangulation of the hull cylinders' planar caps (Gouraud interpolation across a cap differs by the diagonal chosen), and the 61-px flame. NOT a substitute for a stored dataset when a policy will be evaluated on official pixels. nvdiff's CPU transform is batch-size invariant to within one float32 ulp at every width, and bitwise at every width on arm64; on x86-64 the clip positions move by one ulp at widths 1-6 and the normals at widths 4 and 8 (CLOSURE-1). Cuda, the certified device, is bitwise invariant at every width. No frame this cell produces is affected: device='cpu' raises. See findings.md section M7 and examples/results/step7/rocket-landing/closure1/.

owed.Craftax.cuda_arm: The comparison arm ran on cpu. Craftax's render is the same torch gather on both devices (no CUDA-only fused kernel), but --device cuda is one flag and should be run on the GPU host with the Craftax GPU suites.
owed.PFRocketLanding.frames: Rocket renders only on cuda through nvdiffrast (CPU refusal is by design), so no frame was produced or compared on this host. OWED to the post-Wave-1 GPU oracle: the 200-state Step-7 reference corpus rendered at 480 px through both trees on one card in one job, byte-compared, plus tests/gpu for this cell. Everything the frame is a function of on the CPU side — the kinematics, the lagged camera, the float64 MVP, the material table, the scene arrays and the checker texture — IS compared here and is identical.
